articles.title: European football: Dortmund win again but Freiburg top after Gladbach rout
articles.summary: Milan come from behind in 2-2 draw with Lazio. Kylian Mbappé strikes twice as Real Madrid cruise. Felix Nmecha scored twice and Fábio Silva grabbed another as Borussia Dortmund won 3-0 at home to promoted Paderborn to continue their perfect start in the Bundesliga.
body: Starting up front alongside Serhou Guirassy for the first time this season, Silva converted a clever pass from the Guinean to give the hosts the lead after five minutes. Guirassy had two goals disallowed for offside in the first half but Dortmund were rarely troubled by the toothless visitors, who are yet to score since returning to the top flight.
Nmecha came off the bench to score twice, wrapping up victory for the hosts with a stunning late bicycle kick.

Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck made his first appearance since picking up an ankle injury at the World Cup and told Sky Germany he kept his comeback under wraps. “We just hadn’t communicated that much yet because I didn’t want to,” Schlotterbeck said, adding “I missed it terribly. It was a serious injury but I’m glad to be back now.”

Freiburg thumped a poor Borussia Mönchengladbach 5-0 at home to climb to the top. Yannik Engelhardt and Igor Matanovic netted twice each and Maximilian Eggestein added a late fifth as the hosts sent Gladbach, who finished with 10 men, to the foot of the table.

articles.title: Guimarães and Saka fire Arsenal to win at Sunderland after Raya spot-kick save
articles.summary: As the final whistle blew Bruno Guimãraes wore a mischievous smile, Enzo Le Fée was a study in dejection and Arsenal’s immaculate start to the season remained unblemished.
body: Two minutes after David Raya had, rather majestically, saved Le Fée’s second half penalty, Guimarães delighted both his new north London, public and plenty of old friends in Newcastle by sending a shot curving past Robin Roefs.

Yet no one should be deceived by the emphasis lent to the scoreline by Bukayo Saka’s stoppage-time penalty and Reinildo’s sending off, this was the toughest of tests for Mikel Arteta’s team. If Sunderland can keep playing like this, Régis Le Bris’s players will surely enjoy more good days than bad.

That penalty miss aside, chapeaux off to Le Fée who has, deservedly, made Zinedine Zidane’s provisional France squad for the forthcoming Nations League matches. Sunderland’s attacking playmaker knew another good performance here could only enhance his chances of moving from long list to shortlist and he did not take long to draw a foul and win a dangerous free-kick.

Arsenal’s former captain Granit Xhaka delighted in curling the meanest of dead balls in Dan Ballard’s direction but the home central defender, a one-time Gunners youth captain, could not quite connect.

articles.title: Keely Hodgkinson has to settle for silver as Audrey Werro takes Ultimate gold
articles.summary: Swiss wins $150,000 with dominant display in 800m. Georgia Hunter Bell second to Kazimierska in 1500m. This season has witnessed an extraordinary arms race between three of the greatest female 800m runners in history.
body: There were some in the press seats who wondered whether the brilliant 22-year-old Swiss might be tired and vulnerable, whether Britain’s Olympic champion, Keely Hodgkinson, or the fast-rising Dutch star Femke Broeders-Bol could take advantage. But at these Ultimate Championships in Budapest, Werro proved again she was 2026’s ultimate performer as she took the $150,000 first prize with another dominant display.

Werro’s formula is simple but devastatingly effective. Run the first 200m in a shade over 27sec to take the lead, control the race like a puppet master, and then apply the squeeze in the last 300m. As things stand, no one has an answer.
She applied it perfectly here, to win in 1min 55.88sec, with Hodgkinson second in 1:56.26 and Broeders-Bol a further half a second back in third.

Werro’s statistics during the outdoor season are extraordinary. Since losing to Hodgkinson at the world indoor championships, Werro has won all 14 events she has entered, run four of the 10 fastest times in history, and took gold at the European championships. Indeed, the only time she has failed to cross the line first was when she was tripped up in the semi-finals in Birmingham.

articles.title: De Zerbi says Spurs have ‘mental block’ after wait for league win continues
articles.summary: ‘No wins, no goals scored … it is tough for the players’ Spurs in 17th place after 0-0 draw against Everton. Roberto De Zerbi says his Tottenham players continue to lack physical fitness and must “unblock” themselves in psychological terms after they drew their latest Premier League blank in a home…
body: De Zerbi gave a number of explanations for Spurs’ slow start, chief among them the injuries that a clutch of players sustained on the long-haul pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. He lamented the impact of the World Cup on the return dates of certain players and mentioned how Sávio and Omar Marmoush had signed late in the transfer window.
De Zerbi talked up a positive opening 30 minutes from his players against Everton but accepted they ran out of steam and that there was a psychological problem.

“There is a word in Italian – sbloccarsi – that literally translates as if we unblock ourselves,” De Zerbi said. “[It is] a mental block because four games, no wins, no goals scored … it is tough for the players. The team is extremely strong, we can score goals and we can win games. And then we have to respect the history of the players in their careers. Forget Dominic Solanke and Marmoush – the other players … they didn’t score many, many goals in their careers and we have to find these goals. I think we can do so with the quality of our play.”

articles.title: Sunderland 0 – Arsenal 2: David Raya, Bruno Guimaraes, class
articles.summary: Arsenal made it four wins from four in the Premier League with a hard-fought 2-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light. The Black Cats played a gritty, physical game, but the Gunners gave as good as they got, and battled to the win.
body: The Sunderland crowd greeted Bruno with a chorus of boos when he replaced Myles Lewis-Skelly at halftime. They take their rivalry with Newcastle seriously. Unfortunately, it was very much a “keep booing, it only makes me stronger” moment. You could see from the little smile on Bruno’s face that he was loving it and using it to fuel him. His “I can’t hear you” celebration to the crowd after he’d put one on postage stamp was absolute perfection.

Great call from Mikel Arteta to pull Myles Lewis-Skelly at the break. Everything was off from him — poor touches, cheap fouls — it simply wasn’t his night. The manager also had to swap Jurrien Timber for Ben White, who appeared to have tweaked his groin. Because when Arsenal get one right back healthy, the other gets injured. That’s how it works. Timber was excellent, by the way.

The Arsenal subs that came on later in the second half, Eze, Merino, and Zubimendi, were mediocre to poor. The depth is tremendous but Mikel Arteta has his work cut out for him to keep everyone sharp so that when they are called into action they don’t, say, give the ball away the only two times they get on it like Merino did today.

articles.summary: Bruno Guimaraes's brilliant first Arsenal goal and David Raya's penalty save inspired the Gunners to a 2-0 victory at Sunderland on Saturday to extend a flawless start to their Premier League title defence.
body: Mikel Arteta's men have conceded just once in five games in all competitions but Sunderland had the chance to breach Arsenal's imposing rearguard when Raya tipped Enzo Le Fee 's spot-kick onto the post.
Just over two minutes later Guimaraes silenced the Stadium of Light as the Brazilian smashed into the top corner from outside the box.
Bukayo Saka 's penalty sealed the victory with the final kick of the game after Sunderland defender Reinildo saw a second yellow card for taking down the England international.
Despite the victory Arteta was still seething after the game at the award of Sunderland's penalty for Ezri Konsa 's pull on Dan Ballard.

articles.title: Shelton relishing challenge of first Grand Slam final against Zverev at US Open
articles.summary: Ben Shelton finds himself in unfamiliar territory after reaching his first Grand ‌Slam final at the US Open, with the American now ready to "do it for the USA" when he takes on top seed Alexander Zverev in Sunday's showdown.
body: Shelton is the first black American man to reach the US Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972, and is aiming to become the first home male player to win the title since Andy Roddick in 2003.
He will have a raucous Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd behind him when he takes on German top seed and title favourite Zverev.
Shelton revealed he took advice from Rafael Nadal before his break-out run in New York.
The 23-year-old from Florida beat compatriot Frances Tiafoe to set up a winner-takes-all showdown with Zverev, who dispatched Karen Khachanov.

articles.title: Guimaraes haunts Sunderland as Arsenal continue winning start
articles.summary: Bruno Guimaraes scored a stunning goal two minutes after David Raya had saved a penalty as Arsenal beat Sunderland 2-0 to move above Manchester City at the top of the Premier League.
body: The Black Cats had the chance to go in front when Ezri Konsa was penalised for holding Dan Ballard in the second half but Raya brilliantly tipped Enzo Le Fee's spot kick onto the post.

Just 121 seconds later, Guimaraes, whose every touch had been booed by the home fans due to his Newcastle connections, crashed a stunning strike in off the underside of the crossbar from outside the Sunderland box for his first Arsenal goal.

Arsenal had to withstand late pressure from the home side, with Raya saving well from Nordi Mukiele, but they made the result safe when Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty after Reinildo Mandava was shown a second yellow card for hauling him down.

The victory, Arsenal's fourth in a row in the Premier League and sixth in all competitions, maintains their strong start to the campaign and puts the champions three points above Manchester City, who face Manchester United live on Sky Sports on Sunday.

articles.title: Brits Skupski, Hewett clinch respective US Open doubles, wheelchair titles
articles.summary: There was double success for Britain at the US Open on Saturday, with Alfie Hewett regaining his wheelchair singles title and Neal Skupski finally claiming the men’s doubles crown.
body: Emotional Hewett burst into tears after beating Tokito Oda 6-0 7-6 (7-5) to deny the 20-year-old Japanese star a calendar Grand Slam.
The 28-year-old, who was beaten by Oda in the finals of the French Open and Wimbledon this year, said: "It's taken lot of hard work, a lot of soul-searching at times, a lot of reflecting.

"The Wimbledon pumping was a tough one to swallow. I definitely came away from that one with a lot of regret, took some time off and had a hard, long look in the mirror about who I wanted to be on the tennis court and how I wanted to show up.

"Today I didn't care about the outcome. It was about being a little bit more like 'Alfie' and showing the fight and showing the grit and the desire to go out and play a bit more fearless. I think the performance showed that."

videos.title: Ceremony for the Arrival of the Olympic Flame | Dakar 2026
videos.summary: The arrival of the Youth Olympic flame in September will mark one of the defining moments on the road to Dakar 2026.
body: Following the lighting ceremony in Athens on 10 September, the flame will arrive in Dakar on 12 September before beginning a 30-stop journey across all regions of Senegal. Supported by further local celebrations across the African continent, the tour is designed to bring the Games experience into communities and build anticipation ahead of the Opening Ceremony.
The Dakar 2026 YOG will take place from 31 October to 13 November 2026, bringing together around 2,700 young athletes aged up to 17 across three host zones: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly.
